the proposed model is the best model for the experimental data based on both information theoretic criteria and psychophysical measures.
the model with TVC is the best model in terms of both trial-by-trial fit and psychophysical measures, but the model with SVC is the best model for predicting the psychophysical measures.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model with trial-dependent variance (TVC) is the most appropriate model to describe the behavioral data.
the TVC model is a good candidate to describe learning in a vibrotactive yes/no detection task in rats, and that stochasticity in learning is an important component in this task.
a model with stochastic learning and random response selection is more appropriate than the deterministic models for the experimental data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a probabilistic learning model with trial-by-trial associative variation can be used for predicting behavioral data of a yes/no detection tasks in rats.
a probabilistic dynamics model can be used to explain the behavioral data of animals in a detection task.
the probabilistic learning model with trial-dependent variance could be a useful framework for modeling operant conditioning in the context of psychophysical experiments.
